page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 472 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for tile and integer operations.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show some limitations. Multi-core stress-ng CPU performance is categorized as weak at 3990.17, and uncached memory bandwidth reads and writes are relatively low at 37.14 GB/sec and 25.89 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and static web serving throughput perform in the average range, with Passmark database operations scoring 2890.86 and static web serving reaching 7.8 GB/sec. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with 7B model text generation dropping to a poor 4.5 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-4ds_v6 offers high memory density per vCPU alongside fast local NVMe storage, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage reduces the need for external disk attachments for temporary data. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, in-memory caching systems with moderate write throughput, text processing applications, and single-threaded data manipulation tasks.

Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the CPU supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions.
